findings.title: The member's expected result denies a truncated body that the subject's own recorded predicate says these bytes are, and in doing so excludes every observable RF-2 route the contract leaves open for them
findings.claimUnderReview: The subject asserts, in the member's pass-property field and again in its mutation field, 'This injection is not truncated-body', while the same expected field also states that N=65536 is not pinned as prefix-only RF-2 and that occupancy EV-5 oversize-from-prefix does not apply.
primaryEvidence: The payload recomputes to 00 01 00 00 — a 4-byte big-endian unsigned N of 65536 followed by zero body bytes. Confirmed by direct read: byteLength 4, digest bf5e8ffa51a9e748985800c1d3d7f1a2a6ae7435136593ca8d9637e3f87c699c.

g21-fixture-corpus.v26 — recorded at D-352, dual ACCEPT 0/0, cited by this subject at $.basedOn.fixtureCorpusV26 and pinned in $.recordedInputs — states the predicate verbatim at its $.authoredCatalog.members[0].mutation: 'Truncated-body is N greater than 0 with fewer than N body bytes.' The payload is N=65536, which is greater than 0, with 0 body bytes, which is fewer than N. The subject's bytes satisfy the recorded predicate exactly.

The same recorded v26 mutation walks the identical chain of facts for its own in-bound N and reaches the opposite conclusion from the subject: 'N=1 is not oversize against the quoted preHandshake clause (N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0). Occupancy EV-5 oversize-from-prefix does not apply. The receiver must read the body.' The subject reproduces the first two of those three facts for N=65536 and then, in place of the third, asserts that the injection is not truncated-body.

g21-fixture-corpus.v31 (recorded D-356) shows what the lineage requires to earn that denial: its expected distinguishes itself from truncated-body by a byte fact — 'Body length equals claimed N=1.' The subject asserts the same conclusion with the opposing byte fact, since its body length 0 does not equal its claimed N=65536.
DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md axis E item 29 defines the truncated-bodies limb the same way: 'a prefix N with fewer than N body bytes delivered.'

The quoted preHandshake clause at $.controlFrameEncoding.preHandshakeBoundQuoted, string-exact against control-protocol-contract.v2, refuses only N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0 from the prefix alone. N=65536 is in-bound, so a conforming receiver must not refuse from the prefix; per $.controlFrameEncoding.frame it must read exactly N bytes of body, and it will find none.
findings.impact: The expected field closes all three routes at once: prefix-only RF-2 is expressly not pinned, EV-5 oversize-from-prefix is expressly inapplicable, and truncated-body is expressly denied — while the same field still reports that CC-5 intent types prefix exactly at as RF-2. No conforming receiver can satisfy the result as written. A receiver that correctly accepts the in-bound 65536 prefix and then refuses on the short body is failed by 'This injection is not truncated-body'; a receiver that refuses from the prefix alone is the off-by-one defect (N >= 65536 rather than N > 65536) that the non-pin clauses exist to exclude. The member therefore cannot serve as correct retained conformance evidence for the exact-bound case. This is load-bearing fixture semantics carried in the pass-property field, not editorial wording, and it is the same defect class on which the byte-identical member was rejected at g21-fixture-corpus.v9 — inverted, not repaired: v9 demanded the prefix-only refusal that the bound forbids, and v34 forbids the prefix-only refusal but also forbids the only refusal that remains.
findings.notWhatIsBeingAsked: This finding does NOT ask that the injection be classified as truncated-body, and does not touch its CC-5 limb, its member id, its input-corpus id, or its path. The member stays the CC-5 prefix-exactly-at witness. The defect is that a class exclusion is asserted as though it were a byte fact, when the subject's own bytes satisfy the recorded predicate for the excluded class.
findings.requiredRemedy: A successor must delete the affirmative behavioural exclusion 'This injection is not truncated-body' from $.authoredCatalog.members[0].expected and from $.authoredCatalog.members[0].mutation, together with the $.doesNot and $.failsIf entries that pin it, and replace it with the non-pin the document already uses for the prefix-only question — that the observable refusal route for these bytes is not pinned by this corpus and remains for a later cycle to measure, symmetric with 'N=65536 is not pinned as prefix-only RF-2'. It may additionally record the byte facts the way recorded g21-fixture-corpus.v26 records them for its own in-bound N (N=65536 is in-bound against the quoted preHandshake clause; the receiver must read the body; body length 0 is less than claimed N=65536) without asserting the truncated-body class. Alternatively it may defer the exact-bound member until its delivery construction is pinned, the boundary standing open at OQ-G21-4 in DECISION-PACKETS/D1-plan/G21.md. It must not keep an expected result that excludes every refusal route the contract leaves available for these bytes. Preserve the frozen payload during repair; the bytes themselves are sound and are the construction sanctioned at D1-plan axis E item 27.

g21-fixture-corpus.v9 $.authoredCatalog.members[0] authored that file. Its Stage A reviews were a dual REJECT: the Claude review 'REJECT 2 MUST-FIX CLAUDE-G21FXV9-M-1 CLAUDE-G21FXV9-M-2, 1 SHOULD-FIX CLAUDE-G21FXV9-S-1', the Codex review two MUST-FIX, the first of which is on this exact member and this exact byte relation.

COORD D-301 records the disposition verbatim: 'Frozen g21-fixture-corpus.v9 and g21-fixture-corpus.v10 stay frozen; do not record them as current.' The same entry carries 'Does not pin N=65536 as prefix-only RF-2.'

House practice in this lineage is the opposite of silence. g21-fixture-corpus.v11, recorded at D-301, carried $.basedOn.predecessorV9 and $.basedOn.predecessorV10 with their paths, digests and verdict strings, pinned the v9 and v10 files and their review prompts in recordedInputs, and carried an explicit 'Does not record g21-fixture-corpus.v9 as current after g21-fixture-corpus.v11 is recorded.' g21-fixture-corpus.v33, recorded at D-358, likewise cites every rejected predecessor of its own run — v22, v23, v24, v27, v28, v29 and v32. The subject cites v32 only, and drops the rest.
grep across the subject for 'g21-fixture-corpus.v9' returns nothing; the only trace of that cycle anywhere in the document is the bare directory string at doesNotMutate[14].
findings.impact: A reader of the subject alone cannot see that the member it presents as one remaining injection already has byte-identical bytes on disk, that the corpus which authored them was rejected by both reviewers on this member's semantics, or that a recorded decision ordered that corpus to stay frozen and not be recorded as current. The omission is not merely bibliographic: the unlanded g21-fixture-corpus.v9 MUST-FIX is precisely the surface on which CLAUDE-G21FXV34-M-1 lands, so the missing custody is what allowed the same defect class to be re-presented without being addressed as a landing. It also leaves a later leftover-join remasurement unable to tell from the subject whether fixtures/g21.v9/ and fixtures/g21.v26/ are one witness or two.
findings.requiredRemedy: A successor should add a basedOn entry for g21-fixture-corpus.v9 carrying its path, digest and both Stage A verdict strings, with a role recording that its G21.cc5.prefix-exactly-at-prehandshake bytes are byte-identical to this payload, that D-301 froze it, that it is not recorded as current, and that it is not this artifact's version number; pin that file and its two reviews in recordedInputs; add 'Does not record g21-fixture-corpus.v9 or g21-fixture-corpus.v10 as current.' to doesNot; and state in whatIsAuthored or the member's mutation that the bytes recur at the frozen fixtures/g21.v9/ path. It should record how it lands or declines the frozen v9 Stage A findings on this member, rather than leaving them unmentioned.
